date_note: Cofense's post gives only its publication day.
title: Cofense: Black Friday-themed phishing email leads victims to a fake Microsoft verification-code page
geo_basis: none: the post names no victim location
summary: Cofense's Phishing Defense Center describes a Black Friday-themed campaign: a German-language email with a link and a PDF attachment leads to a Constant Contact page, then a fake Adobe Acrobat page, then a fake Microsoft verification page on Cloudflare's workers.dev. Cofense says victims are asked to generate a verification code and paste it in, which could give attackers access to their Microsoft account.
plain: Cofense says a fake Black Friday offer email tricks people into creating and pasting a Microsoft login code, which could give attackers access to the account.
exec: Cofense describes a phishing campaign that abuses Microsoft device login codes using shopping-offer lures.
action: Cofense advises confirming promotions on the retailer's legitimate website first, treating unexpected verification requests with suspicion and adding defensive layers beyond employee awareness.

validation.note: Only Cofense's own research post was read; no independent publisher reports this campaign.

review.note: Compared Cofense post: date 2026-11-23, German email, Constant Contact/Adobe/workers.dev chain, device code, advice; single source, severity 1
